verdict.rationale: Stripe's Shared Payment Token docs explicitly describe per-agent-issued tokens with configurable usage_limits (currency, max_amount, expiration) and an explicit revoke capability ('Revoke the SPT at any time to prevent the seller from using it to create a payment... Sellers can't create a payment with a revoked SPT'), backed by a documented state machine (active/requires_action/deactivated) and webhooks for each transition. RAK restricted keys further let sellers scope what an agent can do on the account. missing for 10: independent/hands-on confirmation that revocation is truly instant in production and that limits persist across an agent's full session rather than a single token/transaction.
